main_text.l: NVPTIALIS CONCIO
I. EX CAP. GENES. 2.
Textus explicandus.
DIXIT quoq; dominus
Deus: Non est bonum
hominem esse solum: fa-
ciam ei adiutorium
quasi coram eo. Forma-
tus igitur dominus De-
us de humo cunctis animantibus terræ
& uniuersis volatilibus cæli, adduxit ea
ad Adam, vt videret quid vocaret ea.
Omne enim quod vocauit Adam ani-
mæ viuentis, ipsum est nomen eius. Ap-
pellauitq; Adam nominibus suis cunc-
ta animantia, & uniuersa volatilia cæli, & omnes bestias terræ. Adæ vero non
inueniebatur adiutor oportunus. Immi-
sit ergo Dominus deus soporem in
Adam: cumq; obdormisset, tulit vnam de
costis eius, & repleuit carnem pro ea. Et
adificauit Dominus deus costam, quã tu-
lerat de Adam, in mulierem: & adduxit
eam ad Adam. Dixitq; Adam, Hoc nũc os
ex ossibus meis, & caro de carne mea. Hac
vocabitur virago, quoniam de viro sumpta

page.notes: The initial D is a large woodcut initial; read as "DIXIT". Words "vocaret" and "vocauit" are printed with a tall-s-like mark above the V in the scan and are copied as printed. The final word "pta" is the catchword-like fragment at the foot and is a partial word, kept as printed. The page-level running head is taken from the title line. Greek and Hebrew: none on this page.
